steps.message:
The bug reproduces. `https://evil.example/phish` and `//evil.example/phish` both come back as a 302 to the attacker's host. Two other findings matter for the fix:

- **Non-string values crash after sign-in.** An array or hash `return_to` raises (`ArgumentError` / `UnfilteredParameters`) inside `redirect_to`, so the reader gets a 500 even though the session was already created. The fix needs to fall back cleanly for these.
- **Relative paths are already safe.** Rails prefixes them with the current host, so `/\evil.example` just stays on our site.

Next I'll confirm that `url_from` rejects the dangerous forms and that `raise_on_open_redirects` is on, since that determines what happens if a foreign host ever gets through.

class SessionsController < ApplicationController

  rate_limit to: 10, within: 3.minutes, only: :create, with: -> { render_rejection :too_many_requests }

  before_action :ensure_user_exists, only: :new

  def new
  end

  def create
    if user = User.active.authenticate_by(email_address: params[:email_address], password: params[:password])

end

steps.message: Both files parse. Next I'll widen the probe into a matrix and check every case for the actual property that matters. For each payload, the sign-in should succeed with a session cookie, return no 500, and send the browser to our host. The check mimics how browsers normalise the `Location` header (strip tabs/newlines, treat `\` as `/`) so it catches the tricky forms too.

require "test_helper"

class ReturnToMatrixTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  HOST = "www.example.com"

  # Approximate how a browser resolves a Location header (WHATWG-ish):
  # strip tabs/newlines, treat backslashes as slashes, resolve against current URL.
  def browser_host(location)
    cleaned = location.delete("\t\r\n").tr("\\", "/")
    URI.join("http://#{HOST}/", cleaned).host
  rescue URI::Error
    :unparseable
  end

  CASES = {
    "absolute evil"            => "https://evil.example/phish",
    "http evil"                => "http://evil.example/phish",
    "protocol-relative"        => "//evil.example/phish",
    "backslash protocol-rel"   => "/\\evil.example/phish",
    "double backslash"         => "\\\\evil.example/phish",
    "mixed slash"              => "/\\/evil.example",
    "tab inside protocol-rel"  => "/\t/evil.example/phish",
    "leading tab proto-rel"    => "\t//evil.example/phish",
    "scheme no slashes"        => "https:evil.example",
    "scheme triple slash"      => "https:///evil.example",
    "javascript"               => "javascript:alert(1)",
    "userinfo trick"           => "http://www.example.com@evil.example/",
    "suffix trick"             => "http://www.example.com.evil.example/",
    "fragment trick"           => "http://evil.example#www.example.com",
    "encoded slashes"          => "/%2F%2Fevil.example",
    "crlf injection"           => "/books\r\nSet-Cookie: x=y",
    "null byte"                => "/books\u0000//evil.example",
    "whitespace only"          => "   ",
    "empty"                    => "",
    "same-host absolute"       => "http://www.example.com/1/foo",
    "same-host https absolute" => "https://www.example.com/1/foo",
    "same-host root"           => "http://www.example.com/",
    "relative path"            => "/books/1",
    "relative with query"      => "/1/foo?x=1",
    "garbage"                  => "%%%not a url[[",
    "very long"                => "/" + ("a" * 20_000),
  }

  test "matrix of string payloads" do
    CASES.each do |name, payload|
      post session_url, params: { email_address: "david@example.com", password: "secret123456", return_to: payload }
      host = browser_host(response.location.to_s)
      puts "#{name.ljust(26)} status=#{response.status} signed_in=#{parsed_cookies.signed[:session_token].present?} location=#{response.location.to_s[0,70].inspect} browser_host=#{host.inspect}"
      assert_equal 302, response.status, "#{name}: expected redirect"
      assert parsed_cookies.signed[:session_token].present?, "#{name}: expected sign-in"
      assert_equal HOST, host, "#{name}: left the site (#{response.location})" unless host == :unparseable
      delete session_url
    end
  end

  test "non-string values fall back to root and still sign in" do
    [
      ["array", ["https://evil.example/"]],
      ["hash", { "a" => "https://evil.example/" }],
      ["nested array", [["//evil.example"]]],
      ["indexed hash", { "0" => "https://evil.example/" }],
    ].each do |name, payload|
      post session_url, params: { email_address: "david@example.com", password: "secret123456", return_to: payload }
      puts "#{name.ljust(26)} status=#{response.status} signed_in=#{parsed_cookies.signed[:session_token].present?} location=#{response.location.inspect}"
      assert_redirected_to root_url, message: name
      assert parsed_cookies.signed[:session_token].present?, "#{name}: expected sign-in"
      delete session_url
    end
  end

  test "wrong password with hostile return_to still rejected, no redirect" do
    post session_url, params: { email_address: "david@example.com", password: "wrong", return_to: "https://evil.example/" }
    assert_response :unauthorized
    assert_nil response.location
  end

  test "new page renders for hostile and non-string return_to without error" do
    [
      "https://evil.example/",
      ["https://evil.example/"],
      { "a" => "https://evil.example/" },
    ].each do |payload|
      get new_session_url, params: { return_to: payload }
      puts "GET new return_to=#{payload.inspect[0,40]} status=#{response.status}"
      assert_response :success
    end
  end
end
EOF

steps.message:
The open redirect is closed. A `return_to` pointing at another site is now ignored, and sign-in lands the reader on our own pages.

**The cause:** `SessionsController#create` passed `params[:return_to]` straight to `redirect_to` with `allow_other_host: true`, which turned off Rails' open-redirect protection.

**The fix (two files, no schema or `db/` changes):**
- `app/controllers/sessions_controller.rb`: `create` now redirects to `safe_return_to_url`, which accepts only a String and runs it through Rails' built-in `url_from`. That keeps same-host URLs and relative paths and rejects other hosts, protocol-relative `//host` URLs, and scheme-only forms. Anything rejected falls back to the default. I also removed `allow_other_host: true`, so any future regression raises an error instead of silently redirecting.
- `app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb`: `post_authenticating_url` runs the session fallback through the same `url_from` check. Nothing in the app currently writes that session key, so this is defence in depth.

**Verification:**
- Before the fix, `https://evil.example/phish` and `//evil.example/phish` both redirected the reader off-site after sign-in. Array and hash values crashed with a 500 after the session was already created.
- After the fix, a matrix of about 30 payloads all sign the reader in. Each lands on our host: absolute, protocol-relative, backslash and tab tricks, `https:host`, `javascript:`, userinfo and suffix tricks, CRLF, null bytes, and very long strings. Non-string values fall back to root.
- Deep links still work. A signed-out request to `/books/new` bounces to sign-in, the form carries the link, and posting it returns the reader to `/books/new`. Sign-in with no `return_to` still goes to root, and the transfer sign-in path still lands on root.
- `bin/rails test`: 179 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors, same as the baseline. Brakeman reports zero warnings, and RuboCop is clean on both files.

**Not done:** I didn't add regression tests to the repo, since you asked me not to edit the test suite. My checks were scratch tests in `/tmp`, which I've deleted. I'd recommend adding a few cases to `test/controllers/sessions_controller_test.rb` (an off-site `return_to`, a protocol-relative one, a deep link, and an array value) so this can't regress. I can add them if you want.
